title: 1908 Messina earthquake
summary: A powerful earthquake centred under the Strait of Messina struck southern Italy on 28 December 1908, followed by a tsunami. Messina, Reggio di Calabria and dozens of nearby coastal towns were almost completely destroyed, and more than 80,000 people were killed. Some survivors were relocated within Italy, while others emigrated to the United States.

where.modern_name: Strait of Messina, between Sicily and Calabria, Italy

importance.justification: One of the deadliest earthquakes in European history, with a tsunami, devastating a major Mediterranean region.

audience_note: Mass death from earthquake and tsunami.
